concept: Crypto bot market-data freshness and stream integrity

claims.text: For Coinbase Exchange level2, size is the replacement quantity at the price level, not a delta, and zero removes a level. Binance also instructs consumers to set the new quantity and remove levels with zero quantity; adding these quantities as increments would violate both contracts. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09)

Monitor market-data freshness per symbol and retain both exchange-event and local receive timestamps. EODHD explicitly separates these timestamps and warns that a connected feed can starve individual symbols; Freqtrade incident logs show outdated candles alongside a RUNNING process heartbeat. (medium confidence)

For Kraken book checksum validation, process all price-level updates in a message before calculating the checksum, delete levels with zero qty, truncate to subscribed depth after updates, and preserve price and qty precision with decimal or string decoding. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09)

A market-data silence threshold must account for channel semantics (design inference). Coinbase ticker_batch sends every 5000 milliseconds only if there is a change, while Binance specifies 1000ms updates for 1s klines and 2000ms for other kline intervals. Silence alone therefore needs channel-specific interpretation. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09)

In the February 27, 2025 Freqtrade discussion, maintainer xmatthias explains that an old WebSocket value can reflect either a disconnect or no trades on an illiquid pair. Last-update age alone cannot identify the cause of silence. (low confidence)

Freshness thresholds should follow the exchange, update frequency, asset and consequence of using a stale value. EODHD explicitly labels its example thresholds as non-universal rather than a general safe timeout. (low confidence)

A REST fallback price must retain its own source and timestamp, and should remain distinguishable from a fresh WebSocket tick. EODHD describes REST fallback as a recovery layer rather than proof that the live stream is healthy. (low confidence)

A snapshot-plus-stream order book requires an explicit bootstrap boundary: queue stream messages, obtain the snapshot, discard messages already covered by its sequence, and replay later messages. Binance and Coinbase Exchange document this pattern. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09)

For Binance Spot depth, if incoming `U` is greater than the local update ID plus 1, discard the local order book and restart synchronization. Older updates are ignored; quantities replace levels, and zero quantity removes a level. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09)

Binance warns that a REST depth snapshot covers at most 5000 levels on each side; levels outside the initial snapshot remain unknown until they change. A synchronized local book therefore need not represent every price level. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09)

Treat candle completion separately from candle receipt: Binance kline payloads include start time, close time and x indicating whether the kline is closed. An arriving update can describe the still-open candle. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09)

Coinbase Exchange heartbeat messages arrive every second for subscribed products and include sequence numbers and last trade IDs for detecting missed messages. These are application-level market-feed checks. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09)

Delivery guarantees must be checked per channel: Coinbase Exchange warns that matches messages can be dropped and recommends heartbeat plus REST trade backfill, while its level2 channel documentation guarantees delivery of all updates. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09)

Binance Spot documents planned connection expiry after 24 hours, server ping frames every 20 seconds, disconnection if a pong is not received within a minute, and the requirement to echo the ping payload in the pong. Monitor continuity across these connection lifecycle events. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09)

Hossein Nejati Javaremi describes batching and aggregation as deliberate feed design choices that reduce message volume while adding latency up to a batch interval; clients must not assume each received message is one exchange event. Coinbase Exchange documents a level2 batch feed using the most recent event time in the batch. (medium confidence)

Monitor transport liveness separately from market-data completeness (design inference). Binance documents ping/pong connection checks, while Coinbase supplies heartbeat sequence numbers and last trade IDs to detect missed messages; a healthy connection alone does not establish a complete feed. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09)

Implement order-book integrity checks according to the venue protocol (design inference): Binance prescribes snapshot-plus-buffered-update alignment and gap detection, whereas Kraken documents checksum validation for its book channel. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09)

For Binance Spot, buffer depth events before obtaining the REST snapshot, align the snapshot lastUpdateId with the buffered U/u range, and rebuild the local order book if U exceeds its update ID plus one. Apply quantities as replacements and remove zero-quantity levels. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09)

Coinbase Exchange warns that matches-channel messages can be dropped. It directs consumers to track the last trade ID through the heartbeat channel and fetch missing trades through REST; heartbeats for subscribed products arrive every second. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09)

Coinbase Exchange explicitly describes level2 as guaranteeing delivery of all updates and starting with a snapshot followed by l2update messages. This is a channel-specific documented guarantee; its matches channel separately warns of dropped messages. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09)

Kraken WebSocket v2 book checksums cover only the top 10 price levels regardless of subscription depth. Kraken makes verification optional and permits checking every update or periodically; the documented checksum does not establish integrity of deeper levels. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09)

Measure event age and local receipt gaps as separate monitor signals (design inference). Binance trade payloads distinguish E event time from T trade time and default timestamp units to milliseconds; Coinbase level2 time records the trading-engine event time. Preserve those meanings and units before comparing timestamps. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09)

narrative.documentConcept: Crypto bot market-data freshness and stream integrity
narrative.text: Market-data monitoring must check freshness per symbol and preserve exchange and receive times. Process heartbeats do not establish candle freshness. Snapshot-plus-stream order books require sequence-aware bootstrap and gap handling. Delivery guarantees differ by channel, and a recent candle update may still describe an unfinished candle. Silence can reflect an illiquid market as well as a failed stream, so freshness limits need context. REST fallback values should remain identifiable by source and timestamp. These checks establish whether the bot is consuming timely and coherent market data.
